newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MINERS' UNION EXPECTS 2,000 FOR RALLY

Mining union, the CFMEU, hopes to gain further public support at a mass rally in Sydney this morning for its fight against Rio Tinto over the move to individual contracts at the Hunter Valley Number One mine.
The union is expecting around 2,000 miners to attend the rally and then march on the head office of Rio Tinto - formerly CRA - in York Street.
The union's northern president Mick Watson said he was expecting miners to come from all over the Hunter Valley and other mining districts to show their support for the strikers.
He said it is the union's intention for the protest to be peaceful, to dispel the notion that the strikers are renegades.
CRICHTON-BROWNE: FRAUD CHARGES "POLITICALLY MOTIVATED"
Former West Australian senator Noel Crichton-Browne has vowed to strenuously defend travel-related fraud charges brought against him yesterday, saying his conscience is clear.
Mr Crichton-Browne and Independent Senator Mal Colston will appear in a Canberra court next month.
The Director of Pubilc Prosecutions yesterday confirmed Senator Colston would be charged in relation to his use of travel allowances and frequent flyer points.
Mr Crichton-Browne is charged with fraud involving spouse travel entitlements.
He said he has been kept in the dark about the charges.
CO PRAISES RAAF CAMBODIAN AIRLIFT TEAM
Five RAAF Hercules aircraft involved in the airlift of Australian citizens and foreign nationals from Cambodia have arrived back in Australia.
Crews of the five Australian aircraft carried out the emergency evacuation of more than 450 people from the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh.
Arriving back in Darwin, there was only praise for the more than 100 personnel from the operation's leader, Group Captain Greg Weekes.

Group Captain Weekes said: "The one day for the operation was very slick, a very professional operation done by a highly trained team - predominantly of Air Force people. It just made me so proud to be able to lead them."
With the situation in Cambodia unstable, Australian crews flew six sorties, airlifting hundreds of Australians, as well as Canadians, New Zealanders and Swedes, out of Cambodia to Penang in Malaysia.
CARR SLAMS HUNTER MINE OPERATOR
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has urged Prime Minister John Howard to take action during his visit to Newcastle today to prompt a resolution to the Hunter Valley coal dispute.
Members of the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) will rally in Sydney today, with members from other divisions promising support for their mining colleagues.
Mr Carr said Mr Howard should use his visit to Newcastle to defuse the dispute and help the CFMEU and Hunter Number One mine owner - Rio Tinto - get back on track to enterprise bargaining. - - - -
FOOD POISONING CHARGES DECISION SPARKS ANGER
The parents of a child who died during the Garibaldi food poisoning outbreak in Adelaide have responded angrily to the dropping of some charges in the case.
Four-year-old Nikki Robinson died in February 1995 at the height of the outbreak.

The state's Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) yesterday decided to drop charges of manslaughter against two of Garibaldi's former directors, and its financial controller, on condition Luciano and Philip Marchi plead guilty to a lesser charge of creating risk of harm.
DPP Paul Rofe said further comment is not appropriate, with the case still to come before court.
But Mr Rofe said he has offered to meet victims and their families today to explain his decision.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
